dimensions.name: Protocol & data-shape orientation

evidence.note: Before writing any code, systematically explored env: dumped all task configs and inspected head-1 rows for a representative dataset of every one of the six task types (classification, clustering, retrieval, sts, pair_classification, summarization), confirming row/field schemas.

Deeper schema probing across types — checked pair_classification list-vs-scalar labels, summarization structure, and iterated over ALL clustering datasets specifically to test for hierarchical labels (found flat); verified retrieval qrels and corpus sizes at step 10.

Actively reconciled computed scores against known all-MiniLM-L6-v2 MTEB leaderboard numbers per type (STS12-17, Banking77/IMDB/MTOPDomain, SprintDuplicate/TwitterSemEval, SummEval, clustering) to anchor expected outputs.

Built a mapping of each dataset to its MTEB task and compared each main_score to leaderboard values, but resolved edge cases (summarization per-prediction skip, IMDB off-by-0.05) reactively rather than pre-identifying them — short of level-10 gotcha anticipation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically surveyed configs and data across all six task types before implementing (steps 2-10), confirming schemas and actively probing edge structures like hierarchical clustering labels and pair-classification label shapes, then reconciled computed scores against the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 MTEB leaderboard for each type (steps 27-97) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of level 10 because config-override cataloguing was implicit and several protocol gotchas (summarization skip semantics, classification divergences) were addressed reactively during validation rather than pre-identified from file/leaderboard evidence.

dimensions.name: Per-type / per-dataset milestone structure

evidence.note: Builds evaluate.py as a shared base/encode core first (PYEOF1) then appends one section per task type — a type-segmented decomposition of the build, though driven by code organization rather than a stated milestone plan.

Validates work one task type at a time via run_eval --type (sts, then classification, summarization, pair_classification, clustering, retrieval), cross-checking each against the leaderboard before moving on — matches anchor 5 and adds a per-type done-check.
Plan line 'Run all STS, then other types step by step' is the closest thing to an ordering statement — rough and tactical, not an explicit ordered milestone plan with stated done-conditions.
Treats CLI contract and skip-and-continue as a distinct verification milestone (nonexistent task, results.json preservation), but only at the very end rather than as a planned sub-goal.
37-dataset coverage is only tallied once at the end ('All 37 tasks have results') rather than tracked as running sub-goals throughout — falls short of anchor 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently split the build and validation by task type and confirmed each type (against the leaderboard) before advancing, with a rough fast-to-slow ordering and a late but distinct CLI/skip-behavior check — clearly above anchor 5. However, it never articulated an explicit, upfront ordered milestone plan with per-milestone done-conditions, the sequencing was convenience-driven rather than risk/shared-machinery-driven, and the 37 datasets were tallied only at the end rather than tracked as sub-goals, so it does not reach anchor 8. This places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Self-built correctness verification against leaderboard/spec

evidence.note: As each task type completed, agent recited specific all-MiniLM-L6-v2 leaderboard values (BIOSSES~0.82, SICK-R~0.77, STS12~0.72, SummEval 0.3015) and compared computed scores against them, flagging summarization as off by 0.04.

Continued leaderboard cross-checks for pair_classification (SprintDuplicate 0.9259 vs 0.946 — noted off by 0.02, tolerance-tight) and clustering, showing systematic per-type comparison to external references.

Built an explicit per-dataset reference table with pass/fail marks (IMDB 0.6648 vs 0.6163 ✗, STS16 off 0.07 ✗, MTOPDomain, AmazonMassiveIntent too high), treating deviations as suspect — this is the core of anchor 5/6 behavior.

For summarization, ran targeted experiments comparing per-text vs per-method skip logic and global vs per-text aggregation, isolating the 0.302 discrepancy to cosine_pearson-vs-spearman — genuine protocol-step localization on one behavior.

Several flagged deviations (IMDB, STS16, AmazonMassiveIntent) were rationalized as 'spec-correct, verifier uses its own gold' and left unresolved; verification focused on main_score with little secondary-metric checking and no disciplined all-37 per-metric loop, keeping it below anchor 8.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly separated the structural harness from a self-built numeric oracle and compared computed main_scores for many datasets against specific leaderboard reference values, flagging large deviations as suspect — solidly at anchor 5. It approached anchor 8 by assembling a per-dataset reference table and localizing at least one discrepancy (summarization) to a specific protocol detail, but fell short: it verified mostly main_score rather than secondary metrics, ran targeted micro-tests only sporadically, and rationalized several unresolved deviations rather than isolating them. This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: 37-task pass/fail tracking

evidence.note: Agent worked through coverage systematically by type (sts, classification, summarization, pair_classification, clustering, retrieval), giving an implicit running list of which task groups were done vs remaining.

Multiple coverage/count checks against results.json (len==37, sorted keys) confirming all 37 tasks present and structurally valid; but this confirmation happened mostly near the end rather than as a continuously maintained ledger.

Built an ad hoc per-task cross-check list vs MTEB leaderboard, marking ✓/✗ for STS and classification tasks — a real coverage/verification pass, but assembled once at the end, not tracked incrementally.

Noticed clear numerical divergences (sts_07 off 0.07, classification_02 off ~0.05, classification_04 too high) but did NOT track them as unconfirmed/failing to fix — rationalized them ('trust the spec') and submitted, so the 'numerically confirmed' status was never accurately maintained.
On retrieval_10 the agent spent many steps passively waiting, but did eventually detect the encoding stall and switch tactics (chunked encoding with progress) rather than looping indefinitely.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept a workable running picture of coverage — iterating type-by-type, verifying 37/37 present and structurally valid, and doing an end-of-run score cross-check — which matches the level-5 anchor (running list of done vs remaining, periodic coverage/structural confirmation). It touches the level-8 behavior by noticing numerical divergences and by detecting the retrieval stall and switching tactics, but it did not maintain an explicit updated ledger of implemented/valid/confirmed states, confirmed coverage mostly at the end rather than continuously, and critically failed to track or re-prioritize the divergent tasks it spotted (rationalizing them away instead). That keeps it at the 5 level rather than higher.

dimensions.name: Debugging protocol divergences

evidence.note: Flags sts_07 as 'off 0.07 ✗' — a 7x-tolerance divergence while all other STS are within 0.01, a strong bug signal — but never investigates or corrects it, just tallies it.

classification_02 (IMDB) off ~0.05: forms hypotheses (kNN vs logreg, sampling, encoding), checks against MTEB source, but concludes 'using the spec correctly' and makes no change despite the large gap.

Summarization off ~0.04: runs genuine variant experiments (per-text vs per-method skip; global vs per-text aggregation), discovers pearson matches leaderboard, and reasons the spearman value is spec-correct — a real hypothesize-test cycle that ends in no correction.
classification_04 flagged 'too high' (0.674 vs ~0.598, ~0.08 off) and left unexamined.

Repeatedly rationalizes divergences ('verifier uses the same spec, so we're correct'), applying tolerance-style reasoning even to 5-8x-tolerance gaps — no protocol root-cause correction ever performed.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent noticed score divergences and, for summarization and classification, formed plausible hypotheses and even ran variant experiments (better than the random-tweak/blame-tolerance behavior of anchor 3). But it never localized a mismatch to a protocol bug and never made a divergence-driven correction — every investigation terminated in 'the spec is correct, the verifier uses the same spec,' and the clearest bug signals (STS16 off 0.07, classification_04 off 0.08) were tallied and rationalized rather than diagnosed. This falls short of anchor 5 (fix and re-check) because no fix followed, but exceeds anchor 3 due to genuine hypothesis-and-test effort, landing at 4.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, high-complexity software task: build an MTEB-style embedding evaluation framework reproducing reference scores for 6 task types across 37 datasets within tight tolerances (1e-2, 3e-2 for clustering). The dev harness checks only structural validity, NOT numerical correctness, so the agent must construct its own correctness signal (spec + public mteb leaderboard) and debug many subtle, easy-to-miss protocol details (shuffle composition, bootstrap oversampling without capping, opposite negation conventions between STS and pair-classification, per-prediction summarization skips). Success requires disciplined orientation, per-type decomposition, self-designed verification, progress tracking across 37 tasks, and iterative correction when scores diverge from the leaderboard.

dimensions.name: Protocol & data-shape orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the six evaluation protocols, the actual shape of the JSONL datasets and task configs, and the MTEB conventions the reference implementation encodes, before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec is dense with per-type conventions and the data/config layout must be inferred from files; acting without inspecting real dataset rows, config fields (min/max_score, overrides, ignore_identical_ids, hierarchical labels), and MTEB scoring conventions leads to silently wrong numbers that the structural harness won't catch.

anchors.0: Starts coding a generic evaluator without opening any dataset file, task config, or re-reading the per-type protocols; assumes a schema.
anchors.3: Reads the spec but inspects only one or two files; misses config overrides (split, seed, samples_per_label, max_fraction, min/max_score) or the corpus title+text rule.
anchors.5: Inspects representative datasets and configs for each task type, confirms row/field schemas, and notes the key per-type conventions before implementing.
anchors.8: Systematically surveys configs and data across all six types, catalogues where configs override defaults, and actively reconciles the spec's stated conventions (negation directions, MRR definition, hierarchical labels) with known all-MiniLM-L6-v2 MTEB leaderboard numbers to anchor expected outputs.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, evidence-backed model of every protocol and its edge cases (identical-id dropping, per-prediction summarization skip, bootstrap k not capped, shuffle composition semantics) grounded in both file inspection and leaderboard cross-reference, pre-identifying the gotchas that will otherwise cause tolerance failures.

dimensions.name: Per-type / per-dataset milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the build into ordered sub-goals (six protocols, 37 datasets, plus the standalone CLI and skip-on-failure harness) each with a concrete done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: 37 tasks across 6 distinct protocols is a natural hierarchy; treating it as one push risks entangling bugs across types and makes it impossible to know which slice is verified. A type-by-type milestone plan with 'reproduces leaderboard within tolerance' as each done-condition is the backbone of steady progress.

anchors.0: No decomposition; attempts to write the whole evaluator in one undifferentiated pass.
anchors.3: Vague ordering (e.g. 'do the easy ones first') with no per-milestone completion criterion.
anchors.5: Splits work by task type and plans to validate each type before moving on, with a rough sense of ordering.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (e.g. STS/retrieval first to establish encode+score plumbing, then classification/clustering/pair/summarization), each with a stated done-check tied to leaderboard agreement, plus separate milestones for the CLI contract and skip-and-continue behavior.
anchors.10: Milestone plan that sequences by risk and shared machinery (build/verify a common encode+similarity core first, then layer type-specific protocols), each milestone gated on a concrete numeric check, with the 37-dataset coverage tracked as sub-goals so no dataset is silently omitted.

dimensions.name: Self-built correctness verification against leaderboard/spec
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing correctness checks — cross-referencing computed main_scores against the public mteb leaderboard and the spec's exact metric definitions — since the provided harness verifies structure only.
dimensions.why_it_matters: This is the crux of the task: the dev signal explicitly does NOT judge numerical correctness, and passing requires all 37 tasks within tight tolerance. An agent that trusts the green structural check will pass structure and fail scoring. Verification must be self-constructed.

anchors.0: Relies solely on run_eval.py structural pass as evidence of correctness; never compares any score to an external reference.
anchors.3: Eyeballs a couple of scores for plausibility but sets no target values and does no systematic comparison against the leaderboard.
anchors.5: Compares main_scores for several datasets against known all-MiniLM-L6-v2 leaderboard numbers and treats large deviations as bugs to fix.
anchors.8: Establishes expected reference values per dataset/type up front and checks computed scores against them within the stated tolerances, verifying not just main_score but the secondary metrics, and isolates disagreements to a specific protocol step.
anchors.10: Runs a disciplined verification loop across all 37 tasks with per-metric tolerance checks, uses targeted micro-tests on tricky sub-behaviors (shuffle composition, bootstrap sampling counts, negation sign per method, summarization skip logic) to localize divergence, and treats the structural harness strictly as a shape gate distinct from its self-built numeric oracle.

dimensions.name: 37-task pass/fail tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which of the 37 datasets are implemented, structurally valid, and numerically confirmed, and detecting when debugging one type is going in circles.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 37 tasks and a pass criterion of all-or-nothing, losing track of which datasets are done/verified (or silently missing from results.json) directly causes failure; long debugging on one protocol can starve the rest.

anchors.0: No tracking; unaware which datasets are covered or whether any are missing from results.json.
anchors.3: Occasional ad hoc mental checks; discovers missing/failing tasks late or by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of tasks done vs. remaining and periodically confirms coverage and structural passes.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of each task's state (implemented / structurally valid / numerically confirmed), notices when a divergence resists fixes, and re-prioritizes rather than looping.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles coverage against the full 37-dataset list and per-metric verification status, proactively flags any dataset not yet numerically confirmed or absent from output, and detects thrashing early enough to switch tactics before burning the horizon.

dimensions.name: Debugging protocol divergences
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation when computed scores diverge from leaderboard/spec, tracing the mismatch to the responsible protocol detail rather than nudging blindly or assuming tolerance drift.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task is full of subtle traps whose only symptom is an out-of-tolerance number; recovering requires hypothesizing which convention is wrong (e.g. capped bootstrap k, wrong negation, non-composing shuffle, missing per-prediction skip) and correcting it precisely.

anchors.0: Ignores or rationalizes score mismatches; ships whatever the code produces.
anchors.3: Reacts to a mismatch with random parameter tweaks or blames tolerance without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: When a score is off, forms a plausible hypothesis about the offending step and fixes it, re-checking against the reference.
anchors.8: Systematically localizes divergences to specific protocol details, corrects the root cause, and confirms the fix didn't regress other tasks; distinguishes genuine clustering drift (3e-2 band) from real bugs.
anchors.10: Runs a tight hypothesize–test–correct cycle on the hardest gotchas, updating its mental model of the reference implementation as evidence accrues, and resolves multiple independent protocol subtleties across types while keeping already-verified tasks green.
